question: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 classified industries in India into _______ categories based on ownership.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Three**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 classified industries in India into **three** categories based on ownership.
 
• **Schedule A (17 industries):** Exclusively under state control and ownership.
 
• **Schedule B (12 industries):** Both state and private ownership were allowed, but the state was expected to assume a dominant role progressively.
 
• **Schedule C (remaining industries):** Left to the private sector, but with the possibility of state intervention if required.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Category I (Schedule A):** This included industries that were to be exclusively owned and operated by the State. These industries were considered crucial for the economy and national security and included sectors like:

 
 
• Atomic energy
 
• Railways
 
• Defense industries
 
• Other key industries such as iron and steel, heavy machinery, and mineral oils.
 
 
 
• **Category II (Schedule B):** These industries were to be progressively owned and controlled by the State but would initially allow both public and private participation. This category included:
 
 
• Fertilizers
 
• Machine tools
 
• Heavy electrical industries
 
• Pharmaceuticals
 
 
 
• **Category III (Remaining Industries):** The third category consisted of industries that were left to the private sector, though the government reserved the right to intervene if needed. These industries were subject to regulatory control but were not the direct responsibility of the state. Examples include consumer goods industries and light manufacturing.
